newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada probably hit lumber exports limit on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Canada probably hit lumber exports limit on Friday.

text.p: Canadian softwood lumber exports to the United States probably reached their quarterly limit late on Friday and any shipments after that will be slapped with an export fee, an International Trade Department source said on Monday.
"It was probably hit late Friday or certainly first thing Saturday," the source told Reuters.

Under an agreement between Ottawa and Washington, export fees will be imposed on Canadian lumber exports exceeding 4.226 billion board feet per quarter or 14.7 billion board feet a year. The agreement became effective on April 1.

At 0745 EDT/1145 GMT on Monday, Canada had officially accounted for export permits 4.093 billion of board feet shipped in the second quarter, which began on July 1. But there is a one-week lag between the entry of lumber in the United States and the application for a permit.
The source said it was unclear by how much the quarterly quota would be surpassed.
"Because of the lag, we are not sure what has actually been exported to the U.S.," the source said.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
